 #   --context-file <path>     Reviewer findings (review only; omit for audit independence)
 #   --model <model>           Dissenter model (default: from config or gpt-5.3-codex)

@@ -145,6 +155,49 @@ _conf_uint() {  # <key (for the message)> <raw> <default> [floor] → a whole nu
   echo "$def"
 }
 
+# cycle-131 FR-4 (SDD D-4.2): flatline_protocol.<gate>.budget_scale (fixed | diff, default fixed) and

+# Grader 1.3.0 (cycle-131 FR-2, SDD §5.2, D-2.1; rule "pm3_or_same_function"):
+#   Citation validity first (both clauses of the new rule): a cited line is positive;
+#   a cited range is ordered (a <= b, the parser orders it); when the defect's file
+#   exists under the head directory the range must lie inside it (1 <= a <= b <= its
+#   line count), else it credits nothing. A cited range wider than 25 lines credits
+#   only through its first line. The two _pm3 results keep the 1.2.0 rule exactly (no
+#   validity rule, no range cap), so recall_pm3_v1 reproduces a 1.2.x grade.
+#   Detection: a valid citation (path, a, b) detects defect d when its path matches d's
+#   file and (i) [a, b] lies within ±3 of any site (unchanged), OR (ii) same scope: the
+#   enclosing definition of the site in head/<file>, identified by its HEADER LINE
+#   NUMBER (never its name), equals the enclosing definition of any cited line in
+#   [a, b]. Definition headers: bash (.sh, .bash, or a bash/sh shebang)
+#   `^\s*(function\s+)?NAME\s*\(\)\s*\{?` and `^\s*function\s+NAME\s*\{`; python
+#   `^\s*def NAME\(`; bats `^@test "…"` plus the bash forms; markdown `#` headings
+#   (the nearest preceding heading's section). A definition runs from its header to
+#   the line before the next header at the same or lower indentation (markdown: the
+#   same or a higher heading level), else to the end of the file, and no further than
+#   its own end (end-of-definition detection): bash and bats — the first `}` line at
+#   the header's indentation (a one-line `f() { …; }` ends on its header); python —
+#   the last line before the first later non-blank, non-comment line indented no
+#   deeper than the def. Nested definitions resolve to the innermost (the latest
+#   header whose definition holds the line); a line after a definition's end and
+#   before the next header is top-level.
+#   Caps: a definition longer than 400 lines, or a file type with no definition
+#   regex (yaml, json, txt, tsv, …), falls back to ±20 lines around the site (and a
+#   cited line in such a definition has no scope); a site outside every definition
+#   (top-level code, text before the first heading) has no scope (±3 only).
+#   Head directory: $EVAL_HEAD_DIR, else <manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head, else

import json, os, re, stat, sys
manifest_path, review_path, executor_path, manifest_v1_path, head_dir = sys.argv[1:6]
man = json.load(open(manifest_path))
man_v1 = json.load(open(manifest_v1_path)) if manifest_v1_path else man
text = open(review_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()

# path:line[-line] citations. Path = something with a file extension; the
# optional trailing range keeps `file.py:10-14` in one token, and the comma
# list after it (`:776,807`) belongs to the same path. A bare `:N` (or
# `head:N` / `base:N`) not glued to a word binds to the most recent path.
# a range dash is unspaced (`a.sh:12 - 40 rows` is prose, not a range) and
# every number ends at a boundary: no letter or digit, and no hyphen / en dash
# before another digit, after it (dates such as 2026-10-05 / 2026–10–05 never
# parse; an open `:369-...` still cites 369) — sprint-250 review run 2, #13
RNG = r'(\d{1,6})(?:[-–](\d{1,6}))?(?![A-Za-z0-9]|[-–]\d)'
CITE = re.compile(
    r'(?P<path>[A-Za-z0-9_./+()-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9]{1,6})[`*)]{0,3}:(?P<first>' + RNG
    + r'(?:[ \t]*,[ \t]*' + RNG + r')*)'
    # head:N / base:N keep the 1.1.0 boundary set ("head:40" binds); the JSON
    # punctuation set, plus a CLOSING backtick (one after a token character:
    # `rows`:40, `"high"`:3), guards only the fully bare :N — an opening
    # backtick (`:7`, (`:212`)) still binds (RG-13) — run 2, #14
    r'|(?:(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:])(?:head|base)|(?<![A-Za-z0-9_./:"\'{}\[\]*])(?<![A-Za-z0-9_"\'}\]]`)):(?P<bare>' + RNG + r')')
ONE = re.compile(RNG)
cites = []
last = None
# the trailer is machine output (its counts are read below), never a citation.
# One pattern strips and reads it (tolerant whitespace, line breaks); the body
# may not contain another comment's `<!--` or `-->`, so an unterminated
# `<!-- LOA-VERDICT` strips nothing — sprint-250 review run 2, #15
TRAILER = re.compile(r'<!--\s*LOA-VERDICT\s*(\{(?:(?!<!--|-->).)*\})\s*-->', re.S)
body = TRAILER.sub('', text)
URL = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://|^//')
for m in CITE.finditer(body):
    if m.group("path") is not None:
        # a URL (https://h/x.js:8080, //host.com:8080) is not a path, nor is a
        # partial match that starts later inside the URL token
        # (https://u@h.com/x.js:8080 matches `h.com/x.js`) — run 2, #11
        # the token so far is the window's text after its last whitespace —
        # one linear split ("" when the window ends in whitespace); `\S*$`
        # also matched before a final newline, so a line-leading citation
        # inherited the previous line's URL, and was O(k^2) — run 3
        tok = re.split(r'\s', body[max(0, m.start() - 4096):m.start()])[-1] + m.group("path")
        if "//" in m.group("path") or URL.search(tok):
            continue
        p = m.group("path").lstrip("(")
        if p.startswith("./"):
            p = p[2:]
        last, spans = p, m.group("first")
    elif last is not None:
        p, spans = last, m.group("bare")
    else:
        continue
    for r in ONE.finditer(spans):
        a = int(r.group(1)); b = int(r.group(2)) if r.group(2) else a
        if b < a:
            a, b = b, a
        cites.append((p, a, b))

def path_matches(cited, defect_file):
    cited = cited.split("head/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("head/") else cited
    cited = cited.split("base/", 1)[1] if cited.startswith("base/") else cited
    if cited == defect_file or defect_file.endswith("/" + cited):
        return True
    return cited == defect_file.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]

# ---- 1.3.0: head files, definition scopes, citation validity --------------------------
RANGE_CAP = 25      # a wider cited range credits only through its first line
SPAN_CAP = 400      # a longer definition falls back to ±FALLBACK around the site
FALLBACK = 20
BASH_HDR = (re.compile(r'^(\s*)(?:function\s+)?[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.:-]*\s*\(\)\s*\{?'),
-----

planted = len(man.get("defects", []))
recall = rate(detected, man)

# refuted share (1.2.0): distinct cited findings that touch no defect site and
# no fix region. Regions are (file, lo, hi) on head/ line numbers, widened ±3.
regions = []
for d in man.get("defects", []):
    for s in (d.get("anchors") or [d["anchor_line"]]):
        regions.append((d["file"], s - 3, s + 3))
for fr in man.get("fix_regions", []) or []:
    try:
        regions.append((fr["file"], int(fr["start"]) - 3, int(fr["end"]) + 3))
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
        continue
findings = sorted(set(cites))
refuted = [c for c in findings
           if not any(path_matches(c[0], f) and not (c[2] < lo or c[1] > hi) for f, lo, hi in regions)]
refuted_share = round(len(refuted) / len(findings), 4) if findings else None

# trailer → severity counts (false positives on clean fixtures)
sev = None
tm = TRAILER.search(text)
if tm:
    try:
        sev = json.loads(tm.group(1)).get("counts")
    except Exception:
        sev = None
if isinstance(sev, dict):
    fp = int(sev.get("critical", 0) or 0) + int(sev.get("high", 0) or 0)
else:
    fp = len({(p, a, b) for p, a, b in cites})
false_positives = fp if planted == 0 else 0

model = effort = None
tokens = None
try:
    ex = json.load(open(executor_path))
    model, effort = ex.get("model_id"), ex.get("effort")
    u = ex.get("usage") or {}
    # every token the call consumed: uncached input, cache writes, cache
    # reads and output — the prompt surface is mostly CACHED input, so
    # input_tokens alone (30 on a real run) would hide the very thing the
    # prompt diet changes
    tokens = sum(int(u.get(k, 0) or 0) for k in
                 ("input_tokens", "cache_creation_input_tokens", "cache_read_input_tokens", "output_tokens"))
except Exception:
    pass

if planted:
    ok = len(missed) == 0
    score = int(round(recall * 100))
else:
    ok = false_positives == 0
    score = 100 if ok else 0

out = {
    "pass": ok,
    "score": score,
    "details": {
        "recall": recall, "planted": planted, "detected": detected, "missed": missed,
        "recall_pm3": rate(det_pm3, man), "detected_pm3": det_pm3, "missed_pm3": mis_pm3,
        "recall_pm3_v1": rate(det_v1, man_v1), "detected_pm3_v1": det_v1, "missed_pm3_v1": mis_v1,
        "planted_v1": len(man_v1.get("defects", [])), "v1_manifest": bool(manifest_v1_path),
        "credits_function_only": function_only, "rule": "pm3_or_same_function",
        "false_positives": false_positives, "severity_counts": sev,
        "citations": len(cites), "model": model, "effort": effort, "tokens": tokens,
        "findings_cited": len(findings), "findings_refuted": len(refuted),
        "refuted_share": refuted_share,
    },
    "grader_version": "1.3.0",
}
print(json.dumps(out))
sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+overlay_answer_paths() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" mode="${3:-head}" tree="${4:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" want="${5:-}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$fixture" && -f "$fixture/head.diff" ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: fixture not found or has no head.diff: ${fixture:-<none>}"; return 2; }
+  case "$mode" in head|base) ;; *) _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: mode must be head or base, got '$mode'"; return 2 ;; esac
+  [[ -d "$tree" ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: source tree not found: $tree"; return 2; }
+  local cs
+  cs="$(_sm_copy_source "$tree")"
+  _sm_evidence copy_source "$cs"
+  if [[ ! "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy source $tree is not a clean git tree (copy_source=$cs)"; return 2
+  fi
+  if [[ -n "$want" && "$cs" != "$want" ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy_source $cs differs from source_commit $want"; return 2
+  fi
+  local out line rc=0
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py overlay "$ws" "$fixture" "$mode" "$tree")" || rc=$?
+  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: the overlay failed (exit $rc)"; return 2; }
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [[ "$line" == *=* ]] || continue
+    _sm_evidence "${line%%=*}" "${line#*=}"
+  done <<<"$out"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_fixture "$fixture"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_source_tree "$tree"
+  return 0
+}

+# check_mount_closed <ws> <fixture-dir> [<source-tree>] [<evidence-file>]
+check_mount_closed() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" tree="${3:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" evf="${4:-${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$fixture" && -f "$fixture/head.diff" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: fixture not found or has no head.diff: ${fixture:-<none>}"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$evf" && -f "$evf" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no evidence file (ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE)"; return 2; }
+  local cs out rc=0
+  cs="$(sed -n 's/^copy_source=//p' "$evf" | sed -n '1p')"
+  [[ "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no clean copy_source in the evidence (got '${cs:-none}')"; return 2; }
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py check "$ws" "$fixture" "$evf" "$tree" "$cs")" || rc=$?
+  if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
+    _sm_err "check_mount_closed: ${out:-the check failed (exit $rc)}"
+    return 2
+  fi
+  _sm_evidence mount_closed "pre-launch ${out#ok }"
+  return 0

+# gates' budget scales with the diff up to USD 6.00. Evidence config_variant=eval.
+apply_eval_config_variant() {
+  local ws="$1" cfg="$1/.loa.config.yaml" g

+  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"

+    G="$g" yq -i '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_scale = "diff" | .flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max = 600' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null \

+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: $g budget keys did not take effect"; return 2; }
+  done

+  return 0

+def cmd_overlay(ws, fixture, mode, repo):
+    if mode not in ("head", "base"):
+        die("overlay mode must be head or base, got %r" % mode)
+    if not os.path.isdir(ws) or os.path.islink(ws):
+        die("workspace not found: " + ws)
+    entries, notes, meta = answer_set(fixture, repo)
+    exp = expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta)
+    for n in notes:
+        note("overlay: " + n)
+    if entries and any(s == "fix" for s in entries.values()) and not meta.get("head_available"):
+        note("overlay: head_commit %s unavailable: fix-commit paths outside the PR are removed" % meta.get("head_commit"))
+    lines, gates, removed = [], [], 0
+    for p in sorted(entries):
+        dst = safe_dst(ws, p)
+        e = exp[p]
+        remove(dst)
+        if e is None:
+            removed += 1
+            note("overlay: removed %s (%s; no %s version)" % (p, entries[p], mode if entries[p] == "pr" else "head_commit"))
+        else:
+            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dst), exist_ok=True)
+            fd = os.open(dst, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | getattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW", 0), 0o755 if e[1] else 0o644)
+            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as fh:
+                fh.write(e[0])
+            os.chmod(dst, 0o755 if e[1] else 0o644)
+            if gate_script(p):
+                gates.append(p)
+        lines.append("overlay_sha256=%s=%s" % (p, state(ws, p)))
+    print("mount_overlay=%s:%d" % (mode, len(entries)))
+    for l in lines:
+        print(l)
+    print("overlay_removed=%d" % removed)
+    print("overlay_fix_commit=%s" % meta["fix_available"])
+    print("gate_scripts_at_pr_version=" + ",".join(gates))
+
+def read_evidence(f):
+    ev = {"overlay_sha256": {}}
+    for line in open(f, encoding="utf-8", errors="surrogateescape"):
+        line = line.rstrip("\n")
+        if "=" not in line:
+            continue
+        k, v = line.split("=", 1)
+        if k == "overlay_sha256":
+            if "=" in v:
+                p, s = v.rsplit("=", 1)
+                ev["overlay_sha256"].setdefault(p, s)
+        elif k not in ev:
+            ev[k] = v
+    return ev
+
+def cmd_check(ws, fixture, evfile, repo, source_commit):
+    if not os.path.isfile(evfile):
+        print("FAIL (a) -: no arm evidence file"); sys.exit(1)
+    ev = read_evidence(evfile)
+    mo = ev.get("mount_overlay", "")
+    m = re.match(r"^(head|base):(\d+)$", mo)
+    if not m:
+        print("FAIL (a) -: mount_overlay=%s (want head|base:<n>)" % (mo or "<missing>")); sys.exit(1)
+    mode, n = m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
+    entries, _notes, meta = answer_set(fixture, repo)
+    exp = expected(entries, mode, fixture, repo, meta)
+    fails = []
+    if n != len(entries):
+        fails.append(("a", "-", "mount_overlay names %d paths, the fixture's answer set has %d" % (n, len(entries))))
+    rec = ev["overlay_sha256"]
+    present = 0
+    for p in sorted(entries):
+        want = sha(exp[p][0]) if exp[p] is not None else "absent"
+        got = state(ws, p)
+        if got != "absent":
+            present += 1
+        if p not in rec:
+            fails.append(("c", p, "no overlay_sha256 line"))
+            if got != want:
+                fails.append(("a", p, "state %s, want %s (%s)" % (got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+            continue
+        if got != rec[p]:
+            if rec[p] == want:
+                fails.append(("c", p, "mount_mutated=%s (pre-run %s, now %s)" % (p, rec[p][:12], got[:12])))
+            else:
+                fails.append(("a", p, "pre-run %s, now %s, want %s (%s)" % (rec[p][:12], got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+        elif got != want:
+            fails.append(("a", p, "state %s, want %s (%s)" % (got[:12], want[:12], mode)))
+    # (b) later-only pinned versions
+    if not has_commit(repo, source_commit):
+        fails.append(("b", "-", "source commit %s not in %s" % (source_commit or "<none>", repo)))
+        later = {}
+    else:
+        known = set(sha(e[0]) for e in exp.values() if e is not None)
+        for t in ("head", "base"):
+            for q in tree_paths(os.path.join(fixture, t)):
+                ff = fixture_file(os.path.join(fixture, t), q)
+                if ff is not None:
+                    known.add(sha(ff[0]))
+        later = {}
+        for p in sorted(entries):
+            tb = tree_blob(repo, source_commit, p)
+            if tb is None or len(tb[0]) == 0:
+                continue
+            h = sha(tb[0])
+            if h in known:
+                continue
+            later.setdefault(h, (p, len(tb[0]), tb[2]))
+        sizes = set(v[1] for v in later.values())
+        scanned = 0
+        if later:
+            for d, dirs, files in os.walk(ws, followlinks=False):
+                rel = os.path.relpath(d, ws)
+                if rel == ".":
+                    dirs[:] = [x for x in dirs if x not in ("pr", ".git")]
+                for nme in sorted(files):
+                    full = os.path.join(d, nme)
+                    try:
+                        st = os.lstat(full)
+                    except OSError:
+                        continue
+                    if not stat.S_ISREG(st.st_mode):
+                        continue
+                    scanned += 1
+                    if st.st_size not in sizes:
+                        continue
+                    h = sha(open(full, "rb").read())
+                    if h in later:
+                        fails.append(("b", os.path.relpath(full, ws), "byte-equal to the pinned %s at %s" % (later[h][0], source_commit[:12])))
+    # (d) the sandbox repository
+    base = ev.get("base_commit", "")
+    gd = os.path.join(ws, ".git")
+    if not os.path.isdir(gd) or os.path.islink(gd):
+        fails.append(("d", ".git", "the sandbox has no .git directory"))
+    else:
+        revs = git(ws, "rev-list", "--all")
+        revs = sorted(set(revs.decode().split())) if revs is not None else None
+        if revs != [base]:
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "commits %s, want exactly the base commit %s" % (",".join(r[:12] for r in (revs or [])) or "<unreadable>", base[:12] or "<none>")))
+        rem = git(ws, "remote")
+        if rem is None or rem.strip():
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "remote(s): %s" % ((rem or b"<unreadable>").decode(errors="replace").split() or "")))
+        if os.path.lexists(os.path.join(gd, "objects", "info", "alternates")):
+            fails.append(("d", ".git/objects/info/alternates", "the sandbox object store borrows another repository's objects"))
+        unr = git(ws, "fsck", "--unreachable", "--no-reflogs", "--no-progress")
+        if unr is None or unr.strip():
+            fails.append(("d", ".git", "fsck --unreachable: %s" % ((unr or b"<failed>").decode(errors="replace").strip().split("\n")[0])))
+        for h, (p, _sz, blob) in sorted(later.items()):
+            if git(ws, "cat-file", "-e", blob) is not None:

+        c, p, d = fails[0]

+if cmd == "answer-set" and len(sys.argv) == 4:
+    entries, notes, _meta = answer_set(sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3])
+    for n in notes:
+        note("answer-set: " + n)
+    for p in sorted(entries):
+        print("%s\t%s" % (entries[p], p))
+elif cmd == "overlay" and len(sys.argv) == 6:
+    cmd_overlay(*sys.argv[2:6])
+elif cmd == "check" and len(sys.argv) == 7:
+    cmd_check(*sys.argv[2:7])
+else:

+# _sm_copy_source <source-tree> → the tree's HEAD (40 hex), "<sha>-dirty" when its .claude/
+# has uncommitted or untracked changes (the copy is then not the commit), else "unknown"
+_sm_copy_source() {
+  local tree="$1" head dirty
+  head="$(git -C "$tree" rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  [[ "$head" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { printf 'unknown'; return 0; }
+  dirty="$(git -C "$tree" status --porcelain --untracked-files=all -- .claude 2>/dev/null | sed -n '1p')" || dirty="?"
+  if [[ -n "$dirty" ]]; then printf '%s-dirty' "$head"; else printf '%s' "$head"; fi
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+overlay_answer_paths() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" mode="${3:-head}" tree="${4:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" want="${5:-}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$fixture" && -f "$fixture/head.diff" ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: fixture not found or has no head.diff: ${fixture:-<none>}"; return 2; }
+  case "$mode" in head|base) ;; *) _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: mode must be head or base, got '$mode'"; return 2 ;; esac
+  [[ -d "$tree" ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: source tree not found: $tree"; return 2; }

+  cs="$(_sm_copy_source "$tree")"
+  _sm_evidence copy_source "$cs"
+  if [[ ! "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy source $tree is not a clean git tree (copy_source=$cs)"; return 2
+  fi
+  if [[ -n "$want" && "$cs" != "$want" ]]; then
+    _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: copy_source $cs differs from source_commit $want"; return 2
+  fi
+  local out line rc=0
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py overlay "$ws" "$fixture" "$mode" "$tree")" || rc=$?
+  [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || { _sm_err "overlay_answer_paths: the overlay failed (exit $rc)"; return 2; }
+  while IFS= read -r line; do
+    [[ "$line" == *=* ]] || continue
+    _sm_evidence "${line%%=*}" "${line#*=}"
+  done <<<"$out"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_fixture "$fixture"
+  _sm_evidence overlay_source_tree "$tree"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# check_mount_closed <ws> <fixture-dir> [<source-tree>] [<evidence-file>]
+check_mount_closed() {
+  local ws="$1" fixture="${2:-}" tree="${3:-${EVAL_PROMPT_TREE:-$_SM_REPO_ROOT}}" evf="${4:-${ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE:-}}"
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$fixture" && -f "$fixture/head.diff" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: fixture not found or has no head.diff: ${fixture:-<none>}"; return 2; }
+  [[ -n "$evf" && -f "$evf" ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no evidence file (ARM_EVIDENCE_FILE)"; return 2; }
+  local cs out rc=0
+  cs="$(sed -n 's/^copy_source=//p' "$evf" | sed -n '1p')"
+  [[ "$cs" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]] || { _sm_err "check_mount_closed: no clean copy_source in the evidence (got '${cs:-none}')"; return 2; }
+  out="$(_sm_oracle_py check "$ws" "$fixture" "$evf" "$tree" "$cs")" || rc=$?
+  if [[ $rc -ne 0 ]]; then
+    _sm_err "check_mount_closed: ${out:-the check failed (exit $rc)}"
+    return 2
+  fi
+  _sm_evidence mount_closed "pre-launch ${out#ok }"
+  return 0
+}
+
+# apply_eval_config_variant <ws> — the cycle-131 evaluation config (FR-4, DEC-0618): both
+# gates' budget scales with the diff up to USD 6.00. Evidence config_variant=eval.
+apply_eval_config_variant() {
+  local ws="$1" cfg="$1/.loa.config.yaml" g
+  [[ -d "$ws" ]] || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: workspace not found: $ws"; return 2; }
+  [[ -f "$cfg" ]] || : > "$cfg"
+  for g in code_review security_audit; do
+    G="$g" yq -i '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_scale = "diff" | .flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max = 600' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null \
+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: yq failed on $cfg"; return 2; }
+    [[ "$(G="$g" yq -r '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_scale' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == diff \
+       && "$(G="$g" yq -r '.flatline_protocol[strenv(G)].budget_cents_max' "$cfg" 2>/dev/null)" == 600 ]] \
+      || { _sm_err "apply_eval_config_variant: $g budget keys did not take effect"; return 2; }
+  done
+  _sm_evidence config_variant "eval"
+  return 0
+}

    inconclusive_by_degradation: "the arm's excluded share > 0.25 (whatever its interval; DEC-0393)"
    investigate: "else any applicable primary has lo > 0"
    keep: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03 and hi < 0"
    inconclusive: "else any applicable primary has d < -0.03, or no valid pair"
    remove: "else every applicable primary has d >= -0.03 and (c <= -15 or w <= -15)"

  inconclusive_extension_trials: 2

      companion_voice)
        _sm_cfg_set_false "$ws/.loa.config.yaml" .flatline_protocol.code_review.companion_voice .flatline_protocol.security_audit.companion_voice \

        ;;

        local k="$ws/.claude/loa/CLAUDE.loa.md" n

        n="$(_sm_drop_md_section "$k" '## Karpathy Principles' "$eval_dir")"
        if [[ "${n:-0}" -eq 0 ]] || grep -q '^## Karpathy Principles' "$k"; then
          _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: no '## Karpathy Principles' section removed"; return 2
        fi
        local cj="$ws/.claude/data/constraints.json" cjn="none"
        if [[ -f "$cj" ]]; then
          # audit r1 DISS-C-008: a failed rewrite is exit 2, not a silent pass; verify afterwards
          jq '(.constraints // []) |= map(select((tostring | test("karpathy"; "i")) | not))' "$cj" > "$cj.tmp" \
            || { rm -f "$cj.tmp"; _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json could not be rewritten"; return 2; }
          mv "$cj.tmp" "$cj"
          cjn="$(jq '[(.constraints // [])[] | select(tostring | test("karpathy"; "i"))] | length' "$cj" 2>/dev/null || echo "?")"
          [[ "$cjn" == "0" ]] || { _sm_err "karpathy_block toggle: constraints.json still carries Karpathy rows ($cjn)"; return 2; }
        fi
        _sm_evidence karpathy_block "removed ${n} lines from CLAUDE.loa.md; constraints.json karpathy rows after: ${cjn}"
        ;;
      rule_files)
        local r gone=""
        for r in stash-safety.md skill-invariants.md; do
          if [[ -e "$ws/.claude/rules/$r" ]]; then rm -f "$ws/.claude/rules/$r"; gone="$gone $r"; fi
          [[ ! -e "$ws/.claude/rules/$r" ]] || { _sm_err "rule_files toggle: $r still present"; return 2; }
        done
        _sm_evidence rule_files "removed:${gone:- none present}"
        ;;
      audit_delta_instruction)
        local s="$ws/.claude/skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md"
        [[ -f "$s" ]] || { _sm_err "audit_delta_instruction toggle: no sandbox auditing-security/SKILL.md"; return 2; }
        _sm_drop_paragraph "$s" "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" \
          || { _sm_err "audit_delta_instruction toggle: no delta paragraph found in the sandbox SKILL.md"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence audit_delta_instruction "removed $(wc -c < "$eval_dir/arm-removed.txt" | tr -d ' ') bytes (.eval/arm-removed.txt)"
        ;;
      loa_mount)
        local p left=""
        for p in .claude CLAUDE.md .loa.config.yaml; do
          if [[ -e "$ws/$p" || -L "$ws/$p" ]]; then left="$left $p"; fi
        done
        [[ -z "$left" ]] || { _sm_err "loa_mount toggle: the sandbox still holds:$left (mount_prompt_surface must be skipped)"; return 2; }
        _sm_evidence loa_mount "none"
        ;;
      effort)
        local f total=0 stripped=0 still=""
        for f in "$ws"/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
          [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
          total=$((total + 1))
          if [[ "$(_sm_strip_frontmatter_effort "$f")" == "1" ]]; then stripped=$((stripped + 1)); fi
          if _sm_frontmatter_has_effort "$f"; then still="$still ${f#"$ws"/}"; fi
        done
        [[ -z "$still" ]] || { _sm_err "effort toggle: effort: still in the frontmatter of:$still"; return 2; }
        local mc="$ws/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" cat_state="absent"
        if [[ -f "$mc" ]]; then
          local nkeys
          nkeys="$(yq '[.. | select(tag == "!!map" and has("default_effort"))] | length' "$mc" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
          [[ "$nkeys" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$nkeys" -gt 0 ]] \
            || { _sm_err "effort toggle: no default_effort key in the sandbox model-config.yaml"; return 2; }

head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:210 — The same-scope clause's bash header regex makes `()` optional-brace and allows `.` in the name, so in any .sh/.bats file it reads every zero-argument call statement as a function definition. That includes Python heredoc bodies (`flush()`, `ds.sort()`, `reader.start()`, `proc.stdout.close()`). The harness files under review are mostly embedded Python. On head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh this gives 13 headers and none of them is a real definition. Lines 842–1916 come out as one "long" scope, and lines 1964–2302 as a single "definition" starting at `ds.sort()`. Any citation within those 339 lines credits a defect anywhere in that range. So `recall` (the decision statistic, with pass and score following it) is inflated for exactly this repository's fixtures. Fix: require `\{` or a following-line `{`, disallow `.` in names, and skip heredoc bodies before matching headers.
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:214 — The markdown heading regex is applied to every line, including the inside of fenced code blocks. A shell or YAML `# comment` inside a fence opens a new "section", so the scope of a markdown site is cut short or moved, and the same-section credit becomes arbitrary. Track ``` / ~~~ fences and skip them.
head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135 — When neither EVAL_HEAD_DIR nor <manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head exists, the scope rule and the citation-validity rule fall back to `<workspace>/pr/head`. That tree belongs to the graded agent and the agent can write to it. Editing it (for example, deleting closing braces so the whole file becomes one definition, or padding line counts) changes what the grader credits. The grader should never read graded-workspace content as ground truth: drop this fallback and let clause (ii) credit nothing.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2159 — split_segments treats every `&` as a command separator, including the `&` in the redirections `2>&1`, `>&2` and `&>`. `diff -u pr/head/X .claude/X 2>&1 | wc -l` splits into `diff … 2>` / `1` / `wc -l`, so the SILENT_SINK pipe check never sees `wc`. The count it prints ("12") then becomes a non-empty section with no ranges and marks every defect of the file `oracle_exposed_unknown`. The `>/dev/null 2>&1` forms are mis-split the same way. Agents append `2>&1` all the time, so this produces false oracle exposures, and those exclude cells from the new sensitivity. Treat `&` as a separator only when it is not part of a redirection.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1995 — The KF-046 class 7 exemption accepts a value when its "unit" (the backtick span, else the whole stripped line) is a plain substring of any fixture line that holds the token. A WebSearch query `0xHoneyJar/loa`, a Grep pattern, or a Bash continuation line holding only the repository URL is therefore always exempt. A WebFetch of `https://github.com/0xHoneyJar/loa` is also exempt whenever the PR contains that URL (a README badge or a `repository:` field). These are real probes of the upstream repository, and the scan was built to catch them. Limit the exemption to non-network tools and fields, and require the unit to be more than the bare token or URL (for example, the full fixture line or a minimum context around the token).
head/evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh:566 — The order of steps defeats the closed-mount check for toggled arms. overlay_answer_paths records `overlay_sha256` and the expected versions (line 559). apply_arm_toggles then edits mounted .claude/ files, and check_mount_closed (line 577) compares the result against the fixture version and the recorded hash. a7_effort_medium applies to review-catch and strips `effort:` from every .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md and edits .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml; karpathy_block, rule_files and audit_delta_instruction also edit .claude/. So any PR fixture that touches one of those files fails clause (a)/(c) before launch: infrastructure_error, no phase runs, arm paused. Either record the overlay hashes after the toggles and make (a) toggle-aware, or apply the toggles before the overlay and exempt toggle-owned paths explicitly.
head/evals/harness/lib/sandbox-mount.sh:1038 — Clause (d) is reused post-run by took-effect.sh oracle_closed. There it requires `rev-list --all` to equal exactly the base commit and `git fsck --unreachable` to be empty. Ordinary agent git use during a review (`git stash`/`stash pop`, `git add` then `git reset`, a scratch commit or branch) creates refs or dangling objects and fails the rule. a1_full lists oracle_closed in took_effect, and a took-effect FAIL rows the trial as infrastructure_error and pauses the arm. So harmless agent behaviour is scored as an infrastructure fault and halts the control arm. Post-run, check only for the later-only pinned blobs and remotes/alternates, not for "no other objects".
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1153 — When review rows carry two grader rules (the expected state during the versioned re-grade, where 1.2.x rows read "pm3"), part_split puts every build row into a separate "· rule n/a" partition. No partition then holds both the build rows and any review-catch rows. The grader rule has no effect on hidden_test_pass_rate, yet H1/A4 and the component decisions in every partition lose one of their primaries. The "largest partition" chosen as primary may also be the build-only one. Build rows should go into each rule partition instead of being split off.
head/evals/harness/ablation-report.py:1840 — After the partitioning change, `V["version"]` is a partition key such as `"2 · pin 0123abcd4567 · rule pm3"`. version_value() passes that string through, so JSON `suite_version` (here, line 1852 and line 2130) is no longer a version number for split versions. Emit the version (PART_VERSION) and the partition key as separate fields.
head/evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:393 — dissent_absent_reason / "disabled" are derived from `sandbox/.loa.config.yaml`, which the agent can write during the run. The harness elsewhere treats sandbox copies as tamperable and never reads them. A run whose config was changed to `enabled: false` is classified as a planned absence and is never excluded by the dissent-absent sensitivity. Read the gate's planned state from the harness-side evidence (arm toggles, or a config hash recorded before launch) instead.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:1656 — missed_pm3_v1 maps an id the current key lacks to its position in the v1 manifest, and that position can already belong to a different defect in the current key. Row and report consumers read `dN` against the current key (they validate against the current defects_seeded and build vectors of length current n), so a v1-only miss is charged to an unrelated current defect. Use a distinct label, or drop ids that cannot be mapped.
head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2010 — corpus_sha256 validates the path with read_regular (O_NOFOLLOW, regular file) and then re-opens it with a plain `open(p, "rb")`, which follows symlinks: a check-then-use race on the hashed file. Hash the bytes read_regular returned (read it as bytes), or hash from the same descriptor.
head/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh:20 — The new budget_scale / numeric-anchor paragraph is inserted between the `--budget` and `--timeout` option entries in the usage header, splitting the options list (`--timeout`, `--dry-run` and `--json` now appear under a "Findings" paragraph). Move the paragraph after the option list.
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:1643 — The example writes `budget_scale: fixed` explicitly under both gates. Per the script, a written key (even `fixed`) sets CONF_BUDGET_SCALE_SET and changes the envelope (it adds budget_scale/budget_cents_effective/budget_cents_max and `reason`). A config copied from the example is therefore not "the shipped gate, byte for byte", contrary to the docs. Leave the keys commented out, or say that writing them changes the envelope.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

That includes Python heredoc bodies (`flush()`, `ds.sort()`, `reader.start()`, `proc.stdout.close()`). The harness files under review are mostly embedded Python. On head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh this gives 13 headers and none of them is a real definition. Lines 842–1916 come out as one "long" scope, and lines 1964–2302 as a single "definition" starting at `ds.sort()`. Any citation within those 339 lines credits a defect anywhere in that range. So `recall` (the decision statistic, with pass and score following it) is inflated for exactly this repository's fixtures. Fix: require `\{` or a following-line `{`, disallow `.` in names, and skip heredoc bodies before matching headers.

head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:214 — The markdown heading regex is applied to every line, including the inside of fenced code blocks. A shell or YAML `# comment` inside a fence opens a new "section", so the scope of a markdown site is cut short or moved, and the same-section credit becomes arbitrary. Track ``` / ~~~ fences and skip them.

head/evals/graders/recall-vs-defects.sh:135 — When neither EVAL_HEAD_DIR nor <manifest dir>/../<fixture>/head exists, the scope rule and the citation-validity rule fall back to `<workspace>/pr/head`. That tree belongs to the graded agent and the agent can write to it. Editing it (for example, deleting closing braces so the whole file becomes one definition, or padding line counts) changes what the grader credits. The grader should never read graded-workspace content as ground truth: drop this fallback and let clause (ii) credit nothing.

head/evals/harness/ablation-grade.sh:2159 — split_segments treats every `&` as a command separator, including the `&` in the redirections `2>&1`, `>&2` and `&>`. `diff -u pr/head/X .claude/X 2>&1 | wc -l` splits into `diff … 2>` / `1` / `wc -l`, so the SILENT_SINK pipe check never sees `wc`. The count it prints ("12") then becomes a non-empty section with no ranges and marks every defect of the file `oracle_exposed_unknown`. The `>/dev/null 2>&1` forms are mis-split the same way. Agents append `2>&1` all the time, so this produces false oracle exposures, and those exclude cells from the new sensitivity. Treat `&` as a separator only when it is not part of a redirection.

I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`. The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**: there are 14 findings, and nothing under `pr/` was modified.

I reproduced two of the problems by running the PR's own code. For the rest I traced the logic by reading but did not run it.

**Confirmed by running the code:**
- **The new "same function" grading rule inflates recall** (`recall-vs-defects.sh:210`). It is meant to give credit when a citation lands in the same function as the planted defect. But its pattern for spotting a shell function also matches any plain call with no arguments, like `flush()` or `ds.sort()`. Most of this repo's harness scripts are shell files with Python embedded in them. On `ablation-grade.sh` it finds 13 "functions" and none of them is real. One of them covers 339 lines (1964–2302), so a citation anywhere in that block counts as catching a defect anywhere in it. This feeds the main decision number.
- **The leak detector misreads `2>&1`** (`ablation-grade.sh:2159`). It is supposed to ignore a `diff` whose output only gets counted (`| wc -l`), but it splits the command at the `&` in `2>&1`, so it never sees the `wc`. The printed count then marks every defect in that file as possibly exposed to the agent. Agents add `2>&1` constantly, so this will generate false exposures.

**Found by reading:**
- **Agent-writable files used as evidence.**
  - When the fixture's own copy isn't found, the grader falls back to the copy of the PR in the agent's workspace, which the agent can edit.
  - The row writer decides whether review dissent was turned off on purpose by reading the sandbox config, which the agent can also change.
- **Repo-name exemption is too loose** (`ablation-grade.sh:1995`). It accepts anything whose text appears inside a line of the PR. A web search for `0xHoneyJar/loa` always passes, and so does fetching the repo's URL whenever the PR contains that URL. Those are exactly the lookups of the original repo the check exists to catch.
- **Pipeline order breaks the new closed-mount check for arms with toggles** (`pipeline-run.sh:566`). The check records the PR's files, then the arm's toggles edit them, then it verifies them. The medium-effort arm runs on review tasks and strips settings from every skill file. On any PR that touches one of those files, the trial is refused before anything runs and the arm is paused.
- **The after-run check flags harmless git use** (`sandbox-mount.sh:1038`). It requires the sandbox's git repo to hold nothing but the starting commit, so an agent that runs `git stash` or makes a scratch commit fails it. That gets recorded as an infrastructure error and pauses the full-setup arm that every other arm is compared against.
- **Report partitioning** (`ablation-report.py:1153`, `:1840`).
  - When old and re-graded review results coexist, build-task results are split into a group of their own, so no group holds both kinds. Every decision in every group loses one of its two measures.
  - For split versions, the JSON `suite_version` field now holds a label string instead of a version number.

The four lower-priority findings are:
- Old-manifest misses can be mapped onto the wrong current defect.
- The corpus hash re-opens its file in a way that follows symlinks.
- A doc paragraph splits the options list in `adversarial-review.sh`'s help text.
- The example config writes `budget_scale: fixed`, which changes the output, contrary to its own docs.
